verdict.summary: The device card label is passed from the kernel/device context directly as the format string to snprintf; a user-influenced card label containing format specifiers is interpreted by the format engine with no validation or safe-format substitution.

evidence.reason: snprintf's format operand is the runtime OS/device-provided value dev->card_label (produced by v4l2loopback_getdevice(file), line 5, with no trust or sanitization invariant shown in the fragment), so any unconstrained content containing '%' (e.g., '%s%n') reaches the interpretive format engine as directives. The absent one-statement fix is a sink substitution: snprintf(cap->card, labellen, "%s", dev->card_label). A format-bearing card label survives the BLOCK test because no shown check, sanitization, or early return lies between line 5 and the line 13 sink; this is CWE-134 (externally-influenced format string).

assumptions: The destination capacity of cap->card is implied by the fragment's use of sizeof(cap->card) at line 8; the failure claimed here is format interpretation, not length overflow.

dev->card_label is classified as runtime kernel/device-provided data per provenance rule (a)/(d): it is consumed from dev obtained via a shown call (line 5), and the fragment displays no invariant that its contents are format-safe.
limitations: The fragment does not show where card_label is populated (e.g., module parameter or ioctl), so the concrete attacker-control channel is inferred from the absence of any sanitization or literal-format substitution; the vulnerability mechanism itself (runtime data as format string) is fully visible in-fragment.
NULL-deref candidates on dev/dev->vdev were demoted: no in-fragment NULL producer or failure path is shown.
device_nr and capability bit assignments are not findings: device_nr reaches only a literal-format %03d specifier, and capability stores are plain struct-field writes.

verdict.summary: seccomp_rule_add failures other than -EFAULT are silently ignored (and seccomp_rule_add_exact returns are discarded), so the syscall blocklist can be exported with blocking rules missing while setup_seccomp reports success, leaving prohibited syscalls allowed inside the sandbox (fail-open).

evidence.reason: The return status of seccomp_rule_add is only trapped when r < 0 && r == -EFAULT; any other negative libseccomp error (e.g., -EINVAL, -EACCES) is admitted by that guard's admitted set and reaches the next statement unchecked, and the function subsequently exports the BPF filter as though the blocking rule had been installed. The missing one-statement fix is `if (r < 0) return flatpak_fail_error (...)` before continuing. The sink is the unchecked installation of a syscall-blocking seccomp rule; the failure is a fail-open policy gap (missing block for e.g. mount, clone with CLONE_NEWUSER, or ioctl with TIOCSTI) rather than a memory-safety error, matching CWE-754 and CWE-390 as a secondary.

Identical -EFAULT-only status handling in the non-devel blocklist loop leaves failures of the personality/ptrace/perf_event_open blocking rules (the personality protection that allows only the caller's allowed_personality value) unchecked, so those syscalls can remain allowed when libseccomp returns a non-EFAULT negative error while the fragment continues to success.

The return value is discarded entirely; a negative return leaves that socket family unblocked and, because the final GE rule only caps families above last_allowed_family, the function still reports success. A status check on r that aborts setup is absent.

assumptions: seccomp_init is checked with `if (!seccomp)` before every later seccomp_* use, so NULL cannot reach a later call.
all blocklist/allowlist array sizes are handled by G_N_ELEMENTS on declarations quoted in the fragment, so loop indices stay within quoted capacities.

verdict.summary: Unbounded recursion in the XML parser: attacker-controlled XML with deeply nested elements makes xml_parse_node recurse once per nesting level with no depth limit, exhausting the stack and causing a remote denial of service.

verdict.summary: In ReadCINImage, the per-row read size fed to ReadBlobStream is GetBytesPerRow(columns, channels, image->depth), where image->depth comes unvalidated from the file-controlled bits_per_pixel byte (0-255). The destination pixel buffer's capacity is GetQuantumExtent (12 bytes/column for RGB at the 32-bit quantum set at line 374), and the computed extent is discarded at line 378 with no length<=extent check. evidence.reason: ReadBlobStream copies up to 'length' bytes into the heap buffer 'pixels', whose capacity is the GetQuantumExtent result at line 377 (12 bytes/column for RGBQuantum with the 32-bit quantum set at line 374). A depth of 255 yields ~96*columns bytes against a 12*columns capacity, and every shown guard on the path (magick check line 68, size guard line 348, offset check line 359, extent status line 362, quantum_info check line 372, q NULL check line 393) admits this value, so the failure set reaches the sink unconstrained — heap buffer overflow (CWE-787); the absent one-statement fix is a bound such as 'if (length > extent) ThrowReaderException(...)' before the read.

assumptions: GetQuantumExtent (line 377) returns the byte capacity of the pixel buffer returned by GetQuantumPixels (line 386) under ImageMagick's standard quantum semantics (columns * channels * quantum/8).
GetBytesPerRow (lines 379/383) returns ceil(columns * channels * depth / 8), rounded per the MagickTrue pad flag, per its standard definition.
ReadBlobStream writes up to its length argument into the caller-provided buffer.
limitations: The capacity of cin.image.channel[] and of the fixed white_point/chromaticity arrays is not declared in the fragment, so the channel loop (line 128, i<8) cannot be judged out-of-bounds in either direction under the CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE.

The extent-based overflow witness relies on the standard semantics of the unshown callees GetQuantumExtent, GetQuantumPixels, GetBytesPerRow, and ReadBlobStream, applied via their shown call sites as permitted by the call-site analysis rule.
Residual memory-amplification through SetImageExtent for a large file is capped by the line 348 guard and its failure is handled at line 362; it is a robustness concern, not the primary finding.

evidence.reason: sl = strlen(name) (line 142) is entry-point-derived with no shown length cap, and sl == N (N = sizeof shm_data_cur->filename, quoted at lines 150/155/156) is admitted by the guard at line 150 onto the else path; the all-unsigned expression sl - N - 1U then wraps to SIZE_MAX, so &name[SIZE_MAX] is read for N bytes, which is out of bounds of the at-least-(N+1)-byte string region that strlen proves for name and of any realizable object. The absent one-statement fix is excluding sl == N from the tail copy (e.g., using + 1U so the offset at sl == N is 1, or guarding sl > N before the else), making this a reachable attacker-controlled out-of-bounds read (CWE-125, root cause unsigned underflow CWE-191).

sizeof shm_data_cur->filename (lines 150/155/156) is a positive compile-time constant N used both as the guard boundary and the copy length.

The read of ulhandler.total_uploaded at lines 193 and 251 after a failed ul_init (else branch, lines 171-172) is a plausible CWE-457 uninitialized-use candidate, but whether the unshown ul_init writes the field on failure cannot be confirmed from this fragment, so it is not used as a finding.

`scanner` and its fields are non-NULL and `skip_ws` is truthy to reach the whitespace branch.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are fully guarded: the allocation result is NULL-checked before every use, the allocation size is exactly matched to the prefix/run/suffix/NUL copies, tab-stop values are range-validated before use, and line scans are terminated by the NUL and MAXCOL guards. No admitted value reaches an unprotected operation.

Copy volumes match the capacity: the second memmove's end offset is (start_col+len)+(old_len-col+1) = old_len+1, equal to the allocated size; the loop writes len chars into [start_col, start_col+len). Residual ranges for col/start_col/len are bounded by the NUL break (158) and MAXCOL break (160–164), and len is the actual computed tab-run length, so no value admitted by those guards exceeds the capacity. No CWE.

New tab-stop is constrained to [1, TABSTOP_MAX] before the tab math (temp = new_ts - (start_vcol % new_ts), num_tabs += num_spaces / new_ts) and before the final option write, excluding division by zero and wrap-around; the degenerate inputs -1, 0, and oversized values are rejected on every path. No CWE.

In the FEAT_VARTABS configuration the NULL fallback ensures new_vts_array is never NULL when later consumed by tabstop_fromto/tabstop_count/tabstop_first (lines 94–100 and 190–205), and new_ts_str is only dereferenced under its own non-NULL check (line 187). The vim_strnsave length (arg - new_ts_str) equals the digit/comma span already consumed, so it cannot exceed the string. No CWE.

All buffer-line reads are bounded by the NUL-terminator break (ptr[col] == NUL) and the MAXCOL break, both evaluated before any further advance, and after a rewrite col is reset inside the freshly allocated line whose NUL was copied at that position; the inner loop terminates and never reads past the line. The u_save return is checked before proceeding, and its failure path sets new_line = NULL which is caught by lines 144/170 before any use. No CWE.

assumptions: The buffer/option invariants that curbuf->b_p_vts_array is non-NULL when set and curbuf->b_p_ts >= 1 are framework guarantees of the Vim option layer, not override-able from within this fragment; every field actually dereferenced here is either NULL-checked, assigned in-fragment, or consumed through callee semantics (tabstop_count(NULL) -> 0).

The ranges eap->line1..eap->line2 are validated by the command framework before ex_retab is called (valid buffer line numbers, line1 <= line2 or handled range semantics); no dangerous operation in the fragment can be driven outside that contract.
limitations: The two preprocessor configurations cannot both compile; the non-FEAT_VARTABS branch's guard set (new_ts range check) and the FEAT_VARTABS branch's guard set (new_vts_array NULL fallback) were each analyzed under their own configuration, and both are safe.

The analysis treats ml_replace/mch_memmove/alloc per their standard Vim/C semantics (alloc returns NULL on failure; memmove with the shown byte count; ml_replace OK/FAIL leaves new_line either the buffer pointer or the unchanged allocated block), so a hypothetical callee misbehavior is not asserted as a vulnerability.
The visible comment and the non-NULL initializer comment are not credited as protective statements; every credited guard is an executable statement.

If the buffer-line-validity and tabstop-option invariants were violated by an out-of-contract caller, behavior would be unspecified, but no shown statement in this fragment admits such a value to a dangerous operation.

The packet batch contains pb_cnt = dp_packet_batch_size(pb) entries (line 5), so refill indices in [0, pb_cnt) are in bounds.

Whether ipf_is_valid_v4_frag/ipf_is_valid_v6_frag access shared ipf state without holding ipf->ipf_lock at lines 11/14 is unconfirmable from the unshown callee bodies; their standard semantics (packet-header validation) show no such shared-state access.
The return value of dp_packet_batch_refill is discarded, but no shown failure path produces an unsafe batch state, so this is not a status-handling finding.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation (ESP trailer writes at the tail buffer, page-frag registration, pskb_put, and cow-path tail use) is protected by a verbatim guard that survives the BREAK test: the tailroom check (L24), the nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS check (L30), the page-frag refill failure exit to cow (L42-45), and the skb_cow_data failure check before any use of its result (L80-81).

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the cow path: on skb_cow_data failure (L79 returning a negative count) the function exits at out before tail = skb_tail_pointer(trailer) (L82), the trailer write (L86), or pskb_put (L87) can consume a NULL/stale trailer or its tailroom. BREAK test passes: identity — the check constrains the exact nfrags value consumed by the branch; boundary — admitted nfrags >= 0 is exactly skb_cow_data's success set, whose standard semantics guarantee tailen bytes of trailer tailroom; reach — L80-81 execute on every path that reaches the cow sink.

Protective statement for the tailroom path: admits only tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb), so the trailer write at tail (L86) and pskb_put(skb, skb, tailen) (L87) consume at most the verified tailroom. BREAK test passes: identity — tailen is unchanged between the check and both sinks; boundary — the admitted value tailen == skb_tailroom still fits an exactly-tailen-byte write and put; reach — all tailroom-path executions pass through this check.

Protective statement for the page-frag registration: nr_frags is re-read unchanged at L54 into nfrags, and the strict comparison admits only 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1, which is a valid index for __skb_fill_page_desc(skb, nfrags, ...) at L56-57. BREAK test passes: identity (same value, no intervening write), boundary (max admitted index is MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1, inside the frag array), reach (the branch condition gates every execution of the sink).

Protective statement for the page-frag path: a failed or unusable frag refill exits to the cow path before page = pfrag->page (L47), get_page(page) (L48), tail = page_address(page) + pfrag->offset (L50), or the trailer write (L52) executes. BREAK test passes: on refill failure the path is short-circuited before any page use, and on success the standard semantics of skb_page_frag_refill guarantee the allocsize-aligned region is available.

assumptions: skb_cow_data(skb, len, &trailer) success (non-negative return) implies trailer has at least len bytes of usable tailroom and a valid tail pointer — standard kernel semantics.
skb_page_frag_refill(sz, pfrag, gfp) true return implies a contiguous sz-byte region at pfrag->offset in pfrag->page — standard kernel semantics.
esp_output_fill_trailer writes at most the prepared tailen-sized trailer area — standard semantics of the ESP trailer filler.
limitations: tailen (int) has no shown non-negativity constraint; consequences of a hypothetical negative tailen on skb->len/data_len/truesize and refcount_add are not demonstrable because no in-fragment producer can make tailen negative — demoted per the internal-helper provenance rule.
A NULL pfrag->page / page dereference (L48, L50) is not a finding: no statement inside the fragment assigns NULL to these pointers, and the initial state of x->xfrag is unshown.
The exact byte count written by esp_output_fill_trailer is not visible; its bounds rest on the standard OEM trailer-filler semantics rather than a quoted write-size expression.
esph_offset pointer arithmetic (L77, L83) depends on esp_output_encap/skb_cow_data internals unshown in the fragment; no in-fragment evidence demonstrates a stale or out-of-object pointer.

A potentially huge allocsz from skb->data_len + tailen wrap is bounded by the L20 ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE check or routes to the checked skb_cow_data path; no surviving unterminated witness was constructed.

verdict.summary: Entry-point coordinate y has no lower-bound check, so negative y (and y+1 in the below block) reaches gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel and the recursive call with an out-of-domain row index, causing an out-of-bounds write/read in the pixel access.

evidence.reason: Entry-point int y retains its full negative range because the only shown constraint, `if (y >= im->sy) { y = im->sy - 1; }` at lines 16-17, clamps only the upper side. Witness y=-1 with border=0, x=0, sx>=1, sy>=1 passes line 8 (`border < 0` false), line 13 (`x >= im->sx` false), and line 16 (`y >= im->sy` false); the left loop at line 20 enters (`i = 0 >= 0`) and this statement passes row y=-1 to gdImageSetPixel, whose standard semantics write the pixel at row y — outside the [0, sy-1] row domain the fragment itself establishes via the clamp at lines 16-17. No statement between line 12 and this sink excludes y < 0 (the `leftLimit == -1` return at lines 27-28 is evaluated after this write). Absent fix: `if (y < 0) { return; }` (or clamp `y = 0`) before the seek loops. Confirmed out-of-bounds write with an attacker-influenced negative index: CWE-787.

The same unconstrained negative y reaches this read: with y=-1 and x in [0, sx-1], the left loop executes and gdImageGetPixel is called with row -1 on the first iteration, before any branch can skip it; the right-loop read at line 33 carries the identical unchecked y. Capacity/domain is the fragment's own row range [0, sy-1] implied by the clamp at lines 16-17. Absent fix is the same missing `y < 0` guard. Confirmed out-of-bounds read: CWE-125.

The below block is gated only by `if (y < ((im->sy) - 1))` at line 56, which excludes the upper side but admits every negative y. For y=-2 (sy>=1), y+1=-1, so this read indexes a negative row; the recursion at line 63 then passes y+1=-1 back into gdImageFillToBorder, propagating the negative coordinate to the unguarded seek loops. Absent fix: a lower-bound check such as `if (y < 0)` (or `y >= 0`) before the below block. Confirmed out-of-bounds read with an attacker-influenced negative index: CWE-125.

assumptions: The valid pixel coordinate domain is [0, sx-1] x [0, sy-1], derived from the fragment's own clamps `if (x >= im->sx) x = im->sx - 1;` (line 13-14) and `if (y >= im->sy) y = im->sy - 1;` (line 16-17), which treat coordinates at/above the dimensions as invalid and must be clamped.

The witness assumes im->sx >= 1 and im->sy >= 1 for a non-degenerate image; if sy == 0, the clamp at lines 16-17 itself produces y = -1, an alternative in-fragment producer of the same negative-row witness.
limitations: The gdImage struct definition and the pixel-buffer allocation are not shown in the fragment, so the exact heap layout (row stride, pointer arithmetic) is not quoted; the OOB conclusion rests on the coordinate-domain invariant visible in lines 13-17 and 56 combined with the standard row-indexing semantics of gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel.
A NULL im dereference (`im->sx` at line 13) is demoted: no NULL-producing statement or failure path is shown inside the fragment, and a caller-supplied NULL is an out-of-scope contract violation.

Deep recursion (lines 47/63) could in principle exhaust the stack on very large images; no attacker-controlled depth bound is derivable from the fragment alone, so CWE-674/CWE-835 is left as a limitation rather than a finding.
The right-loop sinks at lines 33/36 share the identical missing `y < 0` guard and are covered by the same witness as the left-loop sinks.

verdict.summary: A negative caller-supplied len is admitted by the `remain >= len` branch and assigned to int rlen, which memcpy implicitly converts to a huge size_t, causing an out-of-bounds read/write.

evidence.reason: rlen inherits the full unconstrained int domain of parameter len (no shown constraint bounds len to non-negative), and when line 11's `remain >= len` holds (e.g., len = -1, remain = 0) line 12 sets rlen = -1, which line 20 implicitly converts to a ~4 GiB size_t copy length, overrunning both buf and the source region. The guards at line 11 (`remain >= len`) and line 14 (`remain <= 0`) constrain only remain and line 14 is not on this path, so the guard fails the identity audit (wrong-object drift); the absent one-statement fix is a non-negative check such as `if (len < 0) return EOF;` before the copy. Primary mechanism: signed-to-unsigned conversion of a negative length producing a huge copy size (CWE-195), with the resulting oversized memcpy causing out-of-bounds read/write (CWE-787).

assumptions: dp->pos and dp->logicalSize are ints per the arithmetic at line 10, so remain = logicalSize - pos can be 0 while len is negative, making `remain >= len` at line 11 true.
memcpy's third parameter has standard size_t semantics, so a negative int argument converts to a huge unsigned value (no callee-specific behavior assumed).

verdict.summary: uECC_sign_with_k performs the ECDSA nonce scalar multiplication EccPoint_mult without randomized projective-coordinate (initial Z) blinding: line 27 passes a hard-coded 0 as the initialization parameter, so the ladder's power/timing behavior varies with the bits of the secret nonce k and an SPA/timing attacker can recover the nonce and the private key; the RNG-based blinding with its return-status check that would neutralize this sink is absent.

EccPoint_mult's initialization (4th) argument is a projective-coordinate blinding parameter per its standard semantics; a literal 0 disables randomization.

The side-channel impact assumes an attacker able to measure power/timing during signing (physical SPA/profiling setup); the cryptographic consequence is full nonce/private-key recovery but the channel requires local observation.

An oversized-curve caller (num_n_bits or num_words beyond uECC_MAX_WORDS) would break several indexed operations, but the fragment shows no producer of such a curve and the caller is unshown; per the provenance rules this is not treated as attacker-triggerable in-fragment.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in unix_expandpath: the directory entry name returned by readdir() is copied into the path buffer with STRCPY without any length check, and the combined write of prefix + d_name + remaining pattern can exceed the allocation of STRLEN(path)+BASENAMELEN+5 bytes.

With (s-buf)+STRLEN(path_end) <= STRLEN(path) from the byte-preserving scan loop, the maximal extent (s-buf)+STRLEN(d_name)+STRLEN(path_end)+1 exceeds the quoted capacity whenever STRLEN(d_name) > BASENAMELEN+4; no protective length check appears before the copy, so the missing one-statement fix is a fit check such as 'if ((size_t)(s - buf) + STRLEN(dp->d_name) + STRLEN(path_end) >= (size_t)buflen) continue;'. The survivor is admitted by every guard on the reaching path, so this is a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

After line 150 stores d_name, len = STRLEN(buf) (line 151) and the remaining path_end is appended at buf+len; this extends the same overflow, since the total footprint (s-buf)+STRLEN(dp->d_name)+STRLEN(path_end) is bounded only by STRLEN(path)+NAME_MAX, not by the quoted capacity STRLEN(path)+BASENAMELEN+5 (line 32). The same absent fit check would neutralize it; no shown statement does, so the admitted long-name witness reaches this heap write unblocked (CWE-787).

assumptions: buf capacity is STRLEN(path)+BASENAMELEN+5 per the quoted allocation at line 32.
The scan loop (lines 49-70) copies path bytes byte-for-byte and path_end points at the break position, so (s-buf)+STRLEN(path_end) <= STRLEN(path).
readdir() returns a NUL-terminated d_name of at most NAME_MAX bytes (standard callee semantics).
limitations: The numeric values of BASENAMELEN and NAME_MAX are not shown in the fragment, so the overflow witness is range-level (STRLEN(d_name) > BASENAMELEN+4) rather than numerically pinned; this fragile boundary caps confidence at 0.62.
vim_regfree(regmatch.regprog) at line 204 can receive NULL when EW_NOTWILD is set and vim_regcomp failed; safety depends on unshown callee behavior, so it is not asserted as a finding.
A negative or oversized wildoff (caller-supplied, no shown producer) could make the loop at lines 78-84 walk before buf; no in-fragment producer drives it, so it is not a confirmed finding.
PTR2CHAR(path_end) at line 60 may read up to one byte past the NUL of an invalid trailing multibyte sequence in path; the caller's buffer capacity is unshown, so this is demoted.
Filtered through the BLOCK test: no statement on the reaching path to line 150 excludes a long d_name; the entry-point filter (lines 141-148) constrains only dot-prefix and pattern match, not length.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is constrained by shown statements: the fast-path check (lines 11-12) bounds the returned pointer, the max() growth keeps the memcpy destination at least as large as actions_len, oversized requests are rejected by the EMSGSIZE check (line 17-20), and allocation failure including int-truncated negative sizes is rejected by IS_ERR (lines 26-27). No failing witness survives the BLOCK test; the potential int truncation of next_offset + req_size (line 14) is a robustness concern with no demonstrated OOB.

Protective: any request that cannot fit within MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE after growth is rejected before allocation, so the candidate witness attr_len=0x7FFFFFF0 (req_size approx 2^31, next_offset small) is excluded here (blocks the oversized-request path, BREAK boundary/reach pass).

assumptions: ksize() returns the actual kmalloc allocation size (standard kernel semantics).
nla_alloc_flow_actions(new_acts_size) yields a buffer of at least new_acts_size bytes and returns an ERR_PTR on allocation failure; kmalloc of sizes >= 2^31 fails.
offsetof(struct sw_flow_actions, actions) is >= 0 and the initial *sfa (allocated outside the fragment) has capacity >= offsetof + actions_len, which the shown increment discipline preserves.
limitations: attr_len has no shown call site or constraint; an unconstrained parameter domain alone is not a finding (Phase 1(c)).
MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE's numeric value and the declared type of actions_len are not shown, so overflow of the actions_len += req_size increment (line 36) cannot be confirmed.
NLA_ALIGN's expansion is not shown; standard rounding semantics were assumed for analysis and it is not credited as a protective statement.

The int truncation of next_offset + req_size into new_acts_size (line 14) is a residual robustness gap; every derived overflow lands in a state caught by the shown IS_ERR or EMSGSIZE checks, so an OOB verdict would require unshown callee/caller behavior and is not demonstrated.
The very first allocation of *sfa is outside the fragment; only the shown increment discipline was relied upon for the capacity invariant.

verdict.summary: In the source_from_buf path, buf[ga.ga_len++] = NUL advances ga_len past the appended terminator, so STRLEN(buf + ga.ga_len) starts one byte beyond the NUL and scans uninitialized heap memory, potentially past the growarray allocation; the resulting corrupted len also feeds later buf[len-1] reads and the fgets size.

evidence.reason: Line 31 wrote the NUL at the old ga_len and incremented it (buf[ga.ga_len++] = NUL;), so line 40's STRLEN starts at buf + ga.ga_len, one byte past that terminator; no shown statement initializes or terminates the memory there, so on a sourced-buffer line STRLEN reads uninitialized heap (CWE-457) and a run of non-zero bytes carries the scan past the growarray allocation (CWE-125). The guards at lines 20 and 28 only guarantee capacity (ga_maxlen - ga_len >= n), not content, and the appended NUL is behind the scan start, so they do not constrain the failure. The absent one-statement fix is to write the NUL without incrementing (buf[ga.ga_len] = NUL;) so STRLEN begins at the terminator; the corrupted len can also make the later buf[len-1] accesses and the fgets size out of range.

assumptions: ga_init2(&ga, 1, 250) initializes a garray of 1-byte items; ga_grow returns OK only when ga_maxlen - ga_len >= n, and newly allocated garray storage is not zero-initialized.
fgets non-NULL means at least one character was read and a NUL was written within the passed size; ga_concat copies the payload bytes without appending a NUL.
In the fgets path line 40 is safe: fgets guarantees a NUL within bounds, giving len = ga.ga_len + segment length.
limitations: Line 26 indexes sp->buflines.ga_data with sp->buf_lnum under the line 24 bound check, but the allocation of sp->buflines.ga_data is not quoted in the fragment, so per the capacity rule no confirmed OOB is asserted in either direction.
The exact post-growth capacity of ga depends on the unshown ga_grow body, so the exact first out-of-bounds offset is a range rather than a single quoted number.

Downstream failures (buf[len-1] reads, buf[len-1] = NUL write, fgets size) depend on the corrupted len value from line 40 and are consequences of the same confirmed failure, not independently confirmed sinks.

verdict.summary: In SProcXkbSelectEvents, the per-event bounds guard checks dataLeft against the pre-normalization size (1), then size is set to 2 before dataLeft is decreased, so dataLeft == 2 wraps unsigned and a subsequent event's c16/c32 swaps read past the end of the request.

The guard at line 53 (dataLeft < (size * 2)) admits dataLeft==2 while size==1; line 64 mutates size = 2; line 67 (dataLeft -= (size * 2)) wraps unsigned to 0xFFFFFFFE; the second iteration's line 53 check passes on the wrapped value and this c16 read executes past the request end (capacity derived at line 23). Missing fix: validate dataLeft after size normalization (require dataLeft >= 4 for size-1 events) so that the wrap cannot disable the guard. Primary CWE-125; the unsigned underflow at line 67 is the independent secondary CWE-191.

Unsigned underflow: the guard at line 53 verifies dataLeft >= size * 2 using the pre-mutation size (1 for BellNotify/ActionMessage/CompatMapNotify), then line 64 changes size to 2, so this subtraction removes 4 bytes after only 2 were verified; with the admitted degenerate value dataLeft==2 (residual range from line 23), dataLeft wraps to 0xFFFFFFFE, corrupting the loop's length accounting and enabling the subsequent out-of-bounds read at lines 56-57 / 60-61. Guard-Identity Audit: class (1)/(4) check-then-use/transformation drift between lines 53 and 64-67. The absent fix is a bounds re-check against the actual consumed size. CWE-191.

assumptions: client->req_len is in 4-byte units and req_len * 4 is the byte size of the request buffer (derivation shown at line 23).

assumptions: Packet data and pck_size returned by gf_filter_pck_get_data(pck, &pck_size) are attacker-controlled entry-point input with no shown size minimum.
ctx->hdr_store is a heap buffer whose only in-fragment sizing is hdr_store_alloc (lines 68-70, 304-306, 348-350); its initial allocation is outside the fragment.
mpgviddmx_next_start_code returns -1 or the index of a complete 4-byte start code, so returned positions stay within the scanned buffer.
gf_m4v_parse_config/gf_m4v_parse_frame return GF_EOS on truncated input and otherwise report parse status; frame_started is set at line 522 after a first full frame.
limitations: First writes to hdr_store at lines 129/275 (and 3-byte stores at lines 217/530) have no shown allocation, so whether those writes hit NULL or undersized buffers depends on hidden ctx initialization; those sinks are demoted for missing capacity evidence.
u32 wraparound of hdr_store_size + pck_size (lines 68-70) would be a CWE-190-driven overflow but requires >4GiB accumulation, which has no fragment-visible witness; demoted.

obj_size (line 360) and parser-provided frame size (line 420) exceeding the remaining buffer are guarded only by asserts (lines 366, 450, 459, 534), which do not execute in release builds; the producers are unshown callees, so no in-fragment witness; demoted.
Reads at lines 256 and 492 from hdr_store share the same unshown-capacity issue as the main sink and are demoted to limitations.

No attacking witness survives the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: The dereference of `local` (line 26) is reached only through the success path of find_site_by_name (lines 23-25): `!find_site_by_name(cl.site, &local, 1)` guards the block, and the failure branch returns -EINVAL before the dereference. The BREAK test passes on identity (same `local`, no intervening assignment), boundary (admitted set excludes NULL), degenerate inputs (empty `cl.site`/`cl.type` skip the branch; DAEMON-and-empty goes to find_myself), and reach (guard executes on the only path to the sink). A NULL reaching line 26 would require the unshown callee to return success without setting `local`, which the fragment does not demonstrate; that residual is recorded in limitations.

assumptions: Global `cl` fields and `booth_conf->name` are entry-point configuration data consumed only as `%s` arguments to literal format strings (lines 22, 41) and as lookup/length inputs.
The `#if HAVE_LIBGCRYPT` block executes in the analyzed configuration; gcry_check_version's failure is checked and returns -ENOENT (lines 15-21).
limitations: Capacity of `cl.lockfile` and length of `booth_conf->name` are not declared in the fragment, so the snprintf (lines 40-42) boundary cannot be confirmed; per the CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE this candidate is demoted here.

A NULL `local` on find_site_by_name success would require an unshown callee contract violation (success without setting the out-parameter); the fragment does not display such a failure path, so it cannot support a CWE-476 verdict.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds write into the triggeredTopics array: the only bound on numTriggeredTopics is the entry-time `== 64` drain check (line 3), while the loop body and tail increment the counter (lines 29/53) without re-checking; an attacker-controlled topic with enough segments drives the index to 64+, writing past the 64-slot array.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds array write (CWE-787): the sink indexes triggeredTopics with numTriggeredTopics before incrementing it, with no bound or drain check immediately before the write. The only shown constraint on the counter is the entry-time guard at line 3 (`if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) { drain(); }`), which executes once before the loop; check-then-use drift applies because the counter is modified at line 29 (and line 53) after that check with no re-check on the sequential loop path. The capacity is the 64 slots evidenced by the drain-at-64 invariant in the comment (line 2) and guard (line 3), so a first write at index 64 is out of bounds. Surviv-ing witness: entry counter < 64 and a topic (entry-point string_view, no length cap shown) with 65+ '/' segments, each passing the untriggered terminating-wildcard-child conditions at lines 24/28, increments the counter past 64 within one call; the BLOCK test finds no intervening statement that re-drains or bounds the counter between that check and this write (recursive entries at line 36 re-check only their own frames). The absent one-statement fix is a drain/bound re-check (`if (numTriggeredTopics >= 64) drain();`) immediately before each `triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++]` write at lines 29 and 53.

Second out-of-bounds write sink (CWE-787), reached on the exact-match tail path: the same counter numTriggeredTopics is incremented with no protective bound before the write, and the only guard, the entry-time `numTriggeredTopics == 64` drain (line 3), does not execute after the loop's increments. The identical witness (long attacker-controlled topic driving the counter to 64+) is admitted by every shown guard on the path, and the missing fix (drain/bound re-check before the write) is absent, so this sink also resolves ABSENT.

assumptions: triggeredTopics has 64 slots, inferred from the fragment's own drain-at-64 invariant (`if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) drain();`, lines 2-3) and the comment 'If we already have 64 triggered topics'; the array declaration is not shown in the fragment.
drain() empties the triggered-topics store; this is not required for the decisive witness, which uses increments from a counter below 64.
A topic path can pass through multiple nodes whose terminatingWildcardChild exists and is initially untriggered (conditions visible at lines 24 and 28), allowing one increment per segment.
limitations: topic.substr(start, stop - start) (line 10) can throw/read on start > topic.size(), but that requires an unshown initial caller passing start > size; the shown recursive caller (line 36) keeps start <= size, so no in-fragment witness exists.
NULL dereference of iterator / it->second is not confirmed: no statement inside the fragment assigns NULL or produces a failure path that yields NULL.
iterator->messages[messageId] (lines 25/49): the type and capacity of messages and the provenance of messageId are not shown, so no OOB verdict is possible.

The triggeredTopics capacity (64) is inferred from the drain guard rather than a quoted declaration; under the strictest capacity-evidence reading the OOB claim would be demoted, which lowers confidence.
Recursion depth is linear in topic length and the loop provably terminates; deep-recursion stack exhaustion on a huge topic is a robustness concern, not a confirmed non-termination finding.

verdict.summary: parse_query copies the DNS type and class with pj_memcpy at p = start + name_part_len without any shown check that p (and p+2) stay within the packet bound max, so an attacker-crafted query whose name ends at the packet boundary causes an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: p is set on line 23 to start + name_part_len, where name_part_len is attacker-controlled packet data returned by get_name_len (line 10) with no shown constraint relating it to max; the only prior guards (lines 11-12, 20-21) check get_name_len/get_name status, not p's position, so a name ending at or within 2 bytes of max leaves p + 2 > max and memcpy reads 2 bytes beyond the packet buffer (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is a remaining-length check before the read, e.g., if (p + 2 > max) return PJ_ETOOSMALL;.

After the line 26 read, p advances by 2 (line 28) with no re-check against max, so this second 2-byte read at attacker-controlled p can equally extend past the packet end (CWE-125); the same absent remaining-length guard is the missing fix.

assumptions: pkt/start/max delimit an attacker-controlled DNS packet buffer, and name_part_len is the name length returned by get_name_len.
start + name_part_len can reach max or max-1 because no shown guard bounds name_part_len against the remaining packet size.
limitations: The write into q->name.ptr (capacity name_len+4, line 15) occurs inside the unshown get_name body; no standard semantics prove it writes more than name_len+4 bytes, so that OOB-write candidate is demoted.
*parsed_len = (int)(p - start) at line 35 computes a pointer difference over possibly out-of-bounds pointers, but its impact is subordinate to the line 26/31 over-reads.
pj_pool_alloc returning NULL is not treated as a failure: its standard semantics never return NULL and q->name.ptr is not dereferenced in this fragment.

evidence.reason: m_ucCount is an unvalidated file-header-derived component count consumed by for(cx = 0;cx < m_ucCount;cx++) at line 30; its only shown bound, assert(m_ucCount < 4) at line 26, is debug-only and never executes in release builds, leaving the residual range 0..255; with m_ucCount = 5 the loop admits cx = 4 and writes past the 4-element struct Line *line[4] declared at line 6 (valid indices 0..3), a stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); the absent one-statement fix is an executable runtime check such as if (m_ucCount > 4) return false; before the loop.

The same unconstrained m_ucCount (only debug-only assert at line 26) admits cx = 4 in this run-mode loop at line 72, so lp[cx] reads past LONG *lp[4] (declared line 37, capacity 4) and a[cx] reads past LONG a[4] (declared line 48), and the dereference writes through an out-of-bounds pointer value — an OOB write (CWE-787) at an independent sink that the missing runtime component-count bound would also prevent.

m_ucCount, m_ulWidth[0], m_ulRemaining[0], m_lRunIndex[0], m_lLimit and m_lJ are treated as entry-point file-header-derived state because the fragment consumes them with no shown validation.

A NULL dereference of CurrentLine() or line[cx]->m_pNext is not a finding: the fragment shows no NULL-producing statement with a visible failure path.

The OOB dimension is not confirmable because the capacity of conn->raddr.addr is not declared in the fragment (recorded in notes.limitations), so no in-fragment witness exceeds a quoted bound.

The macro write into portstr at line 173 is not analyzable because UNIXSOCK_PATH's expansion is unshown; that write cannot support a finding in either direction and is recorded in notes.limitations.

UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN is the path-length capacity constant named in the line-174 guard; the guard admits only strlen(portstr) strictly below it.

A caller passing NULL for c or mrb would be an out-of-scope API-contract violation, not an in-fragment producer.

verdict.summary: FractionalMaxPool/FractionalAvgPool Compute indexes the output matrix with the input batch count: when pooling_ratio_[0] > 1 the output batch dim shrinks (output_size[0] < input_size[0]) yet the b loop still iterates to input_size[0], so out_offset reaches input0*out1*out2-1 while out_mat has only out0*out1*out2 columns, producing a heap out-of-bounds write.

evidence.reason: out_offset (line 103-104) is (b*output_size[1]+hs)*output_size[2]+ws with b in [0, input_size[0]) (line 92) and hs/ws bounded by the pooling sequences, but out_mat's column capacity is output_size[2]*output_size[1]*output_size[0] (line 67-68). The only ratio guard, line 19 'input_size[i] >= pooling_ratio_[i]', admits pooling_ratio_[0]=2.0 with input_size[0]=2, yielding output_size[0]=floor(2/2)=1 (line 29-30); then b=1 is admitted (line 92) and out_offset reaches input0*out1*out2-1 = 2*8*8-1 = 127 while out_mat has 1*8*8 = 64 columns, so out_mat.col(127) writes past the output buffer allocated at lines 46-50 (heap OOB write, CWE-787). Missing fix: constrain the batch ratio (e.g., OP_REQUIRES pooling_ratio_[0] == 1) or iterate b < output_size[0].

assumptions: out_mat column capacity is derived from the verbatim out_mat construction at lines 67-68 and the output buffer allocation at lines 46-50.
GeneratePoolingSequence standard semantics: returns output+1 cumulative boundaries ending at input, so hs/ws iterate output_size[1]-1 / output_size[2]-1 times.
limitations: A separate candidate (unsigned underflow of height_cum_seq.size() - 1 at line 94 if pooling_ratio_[1] <= 0 makes the sequence empty) is demoted because it additionally depends on an unchecked negative attribute sign and the callee's empty-vector behavior, neither fully visible in the fragment.

Output shapes set with unknown or extreme nvals/rank (lines 4-6) are shape metadata only in this fragment; any downstream allocation-time failure would occur in unshown consumers and is out of scope.

verdict.summary: A crafted lossless-JPEG stream makes DecodeRun return a run larger than the remaining line width; the unguarded while(run) write loop overruns the width-derived payload of line->m_pData before the post-loop if(length) check is reached.

evidence.reason: DecodeRun (L53) yields run with no shown upper bound; while(run) (L56) admits any run >= 1 and each iteration writes line 60 into lp, which advances one slot per pixel against the width-derived payload extent of line->m_pData fixed by L32 (LONG length = m_ulWidth[0];) and L33 (LONG *lp = line->m_pData;). When run exceeds the residual length, the write overruns the payload before run--,length-- (L64) turns length negative, and the post-loop if (length) (L70) is evaluated too late and only guards the separate write at L92. No clamp such as 'if (run > length) run = length;' or 'while (run && length)' appears before the sink, and every guard on the path (lines caps L21-L28) constrains a different object, so an attacker-controlled run admitted at L56 reaches an unprotected OOB write (CWE-787).

assumptions: The raster-line payload of line->m_pData holds m_ulWidth[0] samples, derived from the quoted width assignment at L32 and the lp base at L33; lp advances exactly one slot per pixel written.
assert(m_ucCount == 1) (L16) is not credited as a protective statement, but it supports that only component index 0 state is in use.
limitations: The heap allocation/declaration of line->m_pData is outside the fragment, so the OOB claim uses the width-derived payload extent rather than a quoted allocation; confidence is capped accordingly.

Non-termination of while(--lines) from a negative int lines (e.g., m_ulRemaining[0] >= 2^31) is not a finding: no shown producer can generate that value (frame-height parsing is outside the fragment).
m_ulWidth[0]==0 would make the inner do-while write one sample then loop forever (--length becomes -1); zero width is not shown producible.
A NULL dereference via line/line->m_pNext is not a finding: no NULL-producing statement is shown in the fragment.

Same unvalidated m_ucCount driver: with m_ucCount = 5 the same loop bound admits cx = 4, writing lp[4] (capacity quoted at line 34, LONG *lp[4]) beyond its end and reading line[4] (capacity line 6) out of bounds. No executable guard appears between the assert at line 23 and this sink; the absent fix is the same runtime component-count check.

assumptions: line[4] and lp[4] are fixed 4-element local arrays (quoted at lines 6 and 34), and the component loops index them with cx < m_ucCount.
m_ucCount is the JPEG-LS scan component count derived from the untrusted codestream; the fragment itself shows no runtime constraint on it.

Confirmed out-of-bounds write with object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS: the value is admitted by the `>` guard at line 384, and the array capacity of MNG_MAX_OBJECTS elements (valid indices 0..MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1) is derivable from the fragment's own initialization loops (lines 114-118, 326-327) and the `i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS` convention in the CLIP/MOVE handlers. Independent unguarded index: loop_level is read from the MNG LOOP payload (chunk[0], domain 0..255) behind only `length > 4` (line 444), and is then used to index mng_info->loop_active/loop_jump/loop_count/loop_iteration (lines 447, 462-463, 466) and again in the ENDL handler (line 492) with no bounds check anywhere in the fragment. assumptions: MNG_MAX_OBJECTS is the element count of the per-object MngInfo arrays; this is established by the fragment's own fill loops `for (i=0; i < MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; i++) mng_info->object_clip[i]=...` at lines 114-118 and 326-327, and by the sibling guards `(i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS) continue;` at lines 455-456 and 522-523.

Warnings via ThrowMagickException do not abort processing (only ThrowReaderException does), so the non-fatal warning at line 390 does not block the sink.
limitations: The LOOP/ENDL loop_level indexing (lines 446-447, 462-466, 492-495) has no bounds check, but the MngInfo loop-array capacities are not declared in the fragment, so per the capacity-evidence rule this candidate is not decisive (recorded as a second evidence item with reduced confidence).

With pos=-1, l = *decoded_size - pos = size+1 > 0, so the 'l < 0' check does not fire, and d + l = (decoded-1) + (size+1) = decoded + size, so the 'd + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX' check does not fire either (since size <= INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX). The guard therefore admits the value, and memmove writes size+1 bytes with destination d = decoded-1, i.e., it performs an out-of-bounds write to decoded[-1], with the source reaching s = decoded. This corrupts memory before the buffer. The absent fix is a pos >= 0 check before the operation, or a guard on pos itself (e.g., changing the guard to also test pos < 0).

Same path: with pos=-1, decoded[pos] reads decoded[-1], one byte before the buffer, which is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). This occurs before the memmove and is on every path where the delete path executes with pos=-1; the guard at lines 31-32 does not exclude negative pos.

If the mismatch check at line 35 does not fire, decoded[pos] = c writes to decoded[-1], an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) with the same negative index produced by the pos-- / arithmetic-cancel pattern described above.

assumptions: decoded is a writable byte buffer whose size is at most INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX, as evidenced by the guard comparisons 'decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX' appearing in the fragment.
rule is an external (attacker-controlled) byte string terminating at a NUL byte; the loop reads it via *rule++.
limitations: The exact capacity of the object decoded is not declared in the fragment; this analysis relies on the max-size constant INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX that bounds the buffer, so an OOB claim on the upper end is demoted, but the negative index (buffer underflow) is reachable regardless of the exact capacity as long as it is finite.
The alternative negative-length witness (l becoming negative) is dead: the guard 'l < 0' catches it before the memmove.
No format-string vulnerability is present: the %s format is a literal, and the decoded buffer is passed as an argument, not as a format string.

evidence.reason: The loop count `limit` (uint16_t read at line 31 from attacker-controlled payload) is not bounded against the declared message extent `len` (line 1): the only path guards are line 23 (`len == 1`) and lines 26-29 (`len == 4` && limit > 0), which never enforce `4 + 4*limit <= len`. For the admitted values len=8, limit=1, iteration i=1 executes memcpy(data+8, &val, 4), writing bytes 8..11 beyond the 8-byte extent — an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The absent one-statement fix is a length check `if (4 + (limit * 4) > len) return 4 + (limit * 4);` before the loop.

With the same admitted witness (len=8, limit=1) and no guard between line 31 and line 34 constraining `4 + 4*i` against `len`, iteration i=1 reads bytes 8..11 of the 8-byte message extent declared by the `data, len` signature on line 1 — an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: `data[0..len-1]` is the only guaranteed-valid extent of the message buffer, per the declaration `uint8_t *data, size_t len` on line 1.

The reverse protection scan finds no check on this path (the sibling UTF-8 branch bounds via njs_string_offset at line 107; the ASCII branch does not). Absent fix: clamp or validate from to [0, length-1] before line 80. Out-of-bounds read → CWE-125.

With args->from = 0 and args->to = -1, `from += 1` (line 20) and `while (from-- > to)` (line 22) drive the body's from to -1; the guard admits -1, so `njs_is_valid(&array->start[-1])` computes and reads array->start - 1, before the buffer. Guard identity passes (same from, no intervening modification) but the boundary is one-sided, so the guard is insufficient. Absent fix: add the lower-bound check `from >= 0` joined with the existing upper-bound check. Out-of-bounds read before the start of the buffer (CWE-786 variant of CWE-125).

assumptions: Fast-array element validity is [0, array->length), as implied by the in-fragment guard `from < array->length` (line 27) combined with the access `array->start[from]`.

assumptions: MqttPacket_Read returns the number of bytes read and reads at most client->rx_buf_len (standard callee semantics; the buffer capacity itself is not declared in the fragment).

Line 417 decrements it and re-enters the full frame-processing path via goto NEXT_FRAME (line 421), including the CellType switch, SetImageExtent, row reads, and AcquireNextImage/list growth (lines 180-421). Because Frames is unsigned, a crafted value of 0 makes --Frames wrap to UINT_MAX, admitting up to 4.3e9 iterations with no shown cap or validation on Frames, causing uncontrolled resource consumption / non-termination (CWE-400/CWE-835). The witness (DimFlag=16, Frames=0) is admitted by every guard on the path (z checks at 131 admit z=1) and survives the BLOCK test; the absent fix is a bounded cap or rejection of Frames before the back-edge.

No loops are present in the fragment, so Phase 3 has no applicable iteration-bound analysis.

session is non-NULL (no NULL-producing statement is shown inside the fragment).

The absent one-statement fix is a bounds check such as `if (offset + 2 > sz) { break; }` before the read. This is a 2-byte out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

verdict.summary: The header callback reads from the libcurl payload at attacker-influenced offsets with no length check against the delivered byte count: snprintf("%s", ptr+22) and sscanf(ptr+timelimit_header_len, ...) read at/ past the end of the delivered header data when a crafted header ends exactly at the prefix boundary.

evidence.reason: Entry-point header data has delivered length bytes = size*nmemb (line 4) and no NUL terminator is established anywhere in the fragment; line 19's prefix guard admits a header of exactly 22 delivered bytes, so ptr+22 is one byte past the delivered data, and the literal "%s" format reads until a NUL, which the fragment never guarantees. The guard at line 19 fails the Guard-Identity Audit (wrong-bound drift: it constrains the first 22 bytes' content, not the buffer length at offset 22), the absent one-statement fix is a source-side bound (e.g., copying only bytes-22 bytes with a precision specifier or a prior length check), and no statement on the reaching path blocks the witness, giving an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

url->timelimit_header_len is an unconstrained struct field; line 13's strncasecmp guard admits a header whose delivered length bytes (line 4) equals that offset, so ptr+timelimit_header_len lands at or past the end of the delivered buffer and the "%u\r\n" scan reads past it. The guard at line 13 constrains only the prefix content, not the delivered length relative to the offset (wrong-bound drift), the absent fix is a length check such as bytes > url->timelimit_header_len before the sscanf, and the witness (header exactly timelimit_header_len bytes) survives the BLOCK test — an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: The number of delivered bytes in ptr is bytes = size * nmemb per line 4, and no shown statement establishes a NUL terminator or a minimum payload length for the header data.

The branch at lines 19-27 executes only when the header begins with the 22-byte literal "icecast-auth-message: "; lines 13-18 execute only when the first url->timelimit_header_len bytes match url->timelimit_header.
The snprintf destination write is bounded by sizeof (url->errormsg) on line 22; only the source read is unbounded.
limitations: The underlying allocation size of the libcurl buffer backing ptr is not declared in the fragment, so the demonstrated failure is a read at/past the delivered bytes boundary (line 4); a heap out-of-bounds in the strictest sense also depends on unshown buffer layout.

A header shorter than a compared prefix could over-read inside strncasecmp itself, but the attacker cannot force the beyond-boundary bytes to continue the match, so that variant is not developed as a separate finding.
The discarded sscanf return (line 16) leaves limit at its initializer 0 on failure; with no shown failure path this is a logic concern, not a memory-safety finding.

The capacity of the destination `data` is a caller contract not shown in the fragment; no destination-overflow finding is made, and count <= max_data bounds the destination copy length.
No NULL-producing statement appears inside the fragment, so no NULL-dereference (CWE-476) claim is made.

The witness relies on an entry-point state (read_pos > write_pos) that no shown statement produces or excludes; per the provenance rules this is an admissible unconstrained state, not a caller-API violation.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation admits a confirmed failing value: the memcpy size is clamped by min() to max_data and the available range, the only in-fragment NULL assignment to status.buffer is paired with a reset that forces count to 0 so the line 6 guard blocks the dereference path, and all OOB hypotheses lack a quoted capacity line.

Attacker control of the v4l2_device_register_subdev failure path is not demonstrated inside the fragment, so the leak is assessed as a low-severity device-probe resource-leak defect rather than a directly attacker-driven corruption.

All memory-safety guards (NULL check L9-10, kfifo status L13-16, sizeof-bound snprintf L25, register-status L28-29) are present; the sole ABSENT resolution is the missing kfree(state) on the register-failure exit path.

verdict.summary: The STUN ERROR-CODE attribute decoder computes value.slen = attr->hdr.length - 4 with no lower-bound check on the attacker-controlled 16-bit length field, so a wire length of 0..3 is converted to a huge unsigned size that pj_strdup then consumes, producing an oversized copy/out-of-bounds read (plus excessive allocation) while parsing a crafted STUN message.

evidence.reason: The wire-derived attr->hdr.length (set at line 13 via GETATTRHDR, 16-bit unsigned, residual domain 0..65535 with no shown minimum) feeds line 19 unchecked; for length 0..3 the expression evaluates to a negative int (e.g., -4) that is converted to the unsigned pj_size_t value.slen, producing a huge size (e.g., 2^64-4) — CWE-195 signed-to-unsigned conversion. The absent one-statement fix is 'if (attr->hdr.length < 4) return ...;' before this line; the BLOCK test finds no shown statement excluding length 0..3 on any reaching path, so the witness survives.

pj_strdup consumes the unvalidated value (slen huge, ptr into the message set at line 18) and by its standard semantics copies value.slen bytes from value.ptr into a fresh pool allocation, so the admitted degenerate length 0..3 yields a copy far exceeding the attribute's own length-region established at lines 18-19 — an out-of-bounds read of the STUN message and an excessive allocation (CWE-125, secondary to the CWE-195 size defect at line 19). No guard protects this sink either; the same length>=4 check is absent.

assumptions: attr->hdr.length is a 16-bit unsigned wire field populated by GETATTRHDR at line 13, giving domain 0..65535 (PJSIP pj_stun_attr_hdr semantics).

limitations: The declared byte capacity of buf is not shown, so the exact out-of-bounds extent of reads at lines 15/18/22 beyond the buffer end cannot be quantified (CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE); only the huge-size mechanism at line 19 and its consumption at line 22 are confirmed.
The return status of pj_strdup is discarded, but pool-allocation failure is not a shown NULL-producing path with an in-fragment dereference, so it is not a separate finding.

Macro bodies (GETATTRHDR, PJ_POOL_ZALLOC_T) and the value of ATTR_HDR_LEN are unshown and are not credited as protective statements; PJ_POOL_ZALLOC_T failure would be a constant-size allocation, not attacker-influenced.
No loops exist in the fragment; Phase 3 is vacuous.

verdict.summary: The BGP capability parser reads sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) bytes from pnt+3 after only guaranteeing hdr->length+3 bytes from pnt; a crafted capability with hdr->length < sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) (e.g., 0) and a short trailing buffer triggers an out-of-bounds heap read past the end of the packet buffer.

The only guards before this copy, line 18 (pnt + 3 > end) and line 43 ((pnt + hdr->length + 3) > end), admit hdr->length in [0,255] with no minimum and guarantee only hdr->length bytes available from pnt+3. The copy reads sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) bytes (>= 3) from pnt+3, so any hdr->length < sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) with a correspondingly short tail passes both guards and reads past end (e.g., hdr->length = 0 with exactly 4 bytes remaining). The missing one-statement fix is if (hdr->length < sizeof(struct capability_mp_data)) return BGP_Stop; before the memcpy. This is a confirmed out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) from an attacker-controlled residual range admitted by every guard on the path.

assumptions: Line 13, end = pnt + length, defines the readable region as [pnt, pnt+length).
hdr->length is the uint8_t length field of struct capability_header, shown read from the packet at line 40, with declared range [0,255] and no shown lower bound.
struct capability_mp_data holds at least a uint16_t AFI and uint8_t SAFI, so sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) >= 3.

Pointer arithmetic pnt + hdr->length + 3 cannot overflow for realistic bgp_size_t lengths and is not a separate finding.

verdict.summary: The CoRRE decoder's guard multiplies the attacker-controlled 32-bit nSubrects by (4 + BPP/8), wrapping to a tiny value that passes the RFB_BUFFER_SIZE check, after which the loop reads roughly 4 GiB from the RFB_BUFFER_SIZE-capped client->buffer, an out-of-bounds read caused by integer overflow.

evidence.reason: nSubrects is a network-read, byte-swapped 32-bit value (lines 9, 12) with no minimum or maximum validation, so its residual range is 0..2^32-1. With BPP=32 (BPP/8=4), the witness nSubrects=0x20000001 makes the line 19 product 0x20000001*8 wrap to 8, an admitted value since 8 <= RFB_BUFFER_SIZE; ReadFromRFBServer then loads only 8 payload bytes into client->buffer, whose only in-fragment size bound is RFB_BUFFER_SIZE (line 19). The loop at line 24 then executes 0x20000001 times, advancing ptr (line 26) by 4+BPP/8 bytes per iteration and dereferencing lines 25-30 past the 8-byte payload and past RFB_BUFFER_SIZE, an out-of-bounds read; the guard at line 19 is insufficient because it constrains the wrapped product rather than the true count (wrong-bound/transformation drift), and the absent fix is a 64-bit product or division-based bound nSubrects > RFB_BUFFER_SIZE / (4 + (BPP/8)). Primary mechanism: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) caused by 32-bit multiplication wrap (CWE-190).

The only in-fragment cap on client->buffer contents is RFB_BUFFER_SIZE, quoted in the line 19 guard.
limitations: The allocation/declaration of client->buffer and the RFB_BUFFER_SIZE definition are not shown in the fragment; the OOB claim rests on the line 19 cap and the 8-byte payload actually read.

A failing witness (i >= alist->al_ga.ga_len) would require an in-fragment producer that shrinks the argument list via autocommands — only acknowledged in comments (lines 48-50, 177), never shown — and depends on the unshown grow-array allocation capacity; under the Capacity-Evidence Rule and BLOCK test the witness is dead, so this is demoted to a limitation rather than a finding.

verdict.summary: vhost_user_set_inflight_fd consumes attacker-controlled num_queues and mmap_size from the vhost-user message with no validation: the loop indexes dev->virtqueue[i] with i up to 65534 (out-of-bounds read) and advances addr by an unchecked per-queue size so the desc_num stores land outside the mmap region sized mmap_size (out-of-bounds write).

The loop header (line 80, i < num_queues) admits i up to 65534 with no guard bounding num_queues against the vring-array element count, whose declared bound is not quoted in the fragment; an attacker message with a large num_queues drives an out-of-bounds read at line 81. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check (e.g., if (num_queues > VHOST_MAX_VRING || num_queues > dev->nr_vring)) before the loop; mechanism is OOB read, primary CWE-125.

The mapping's capacity is mmap_size, quoted as the length argument at line 64 (mmap(0, mmap_size, ...)) and stored at line 78; mmap_size, num_queues and queue_size are unconstrained entry-point values (lines 21-24). The loop (line 80) runs up to 65535 iterations and each iteration advances addr by pervq_inflight_size (line 92, produced by the unshown get_pervq_shm_size_* helpers, nonzero for queue_size >= 1 by their name semantics), so with a minimal successful mmap_size (e.g., one page) and a large num_queues, the desc_num store at offsets k*pervq_inflight_size falls beyond [addr, addr+mmap_size). Line 66 checks only the initial MAP_FAILED and no loop-path statement re-tests addr against the mapping end. The absent fix is a check that num_queues*pervq_inflight_size <= mmap_size before the loop (or a per-iteration addr recheck); mechanism is OOB write, primary CWE-787.

assumptions: ctx and all ctx->msg.payload.inflight fields are entry-point data from the vhost-user control channel (attacker-controlled).
mmap(0, mmap_size, ...) succeeds for a small nonzero length; only MAP_FAILED is the shown failure path.

The vring array dev->virtqueue has an element count below 65535; its declared bound (VHOST_MAX_VRING) is not quoted in this fragment.
limitations: Per CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE, the declared capacity of dev->virtqueue is absent from the fragment, so the CWE-125 read alone would be demoted; it is retained because the same unvalidated loop also drives the mmap-region overrun whose capacity (mmap_size, line 64) is quoted.
The exact numerical value of pervq_inflight_size depends on unshown helper bodies; the CWE-787 witness only requires it to be nonzero for an attacker-chosen queue_size.
dev->virtqueue[0]->numa_node (line 46) is dereferenced under the nr_vring > 0 invariant, which is not shown in the fragment.
ctx->fds[0] is read before any shown fd-count check; after line 15 the residual fd >= 0, and invalid fds fail at mmap (MAP_FAILED is checked), so no separate finding is asserted.

verdict.summary: disable_priv_mode fails open: after setuid or setgid returns an error the function still unconditionally records the target uid/gid as effective, so the recorded privilege state diverges from the real effective ids while execution continues.

evidence.reason: setgid failure is admitted by the guard `if (setgid (current_user.gid) < 0)` (L14) and the branch only calls sys_error (L15), whose shown text contains no exit or return; execution falls through to the unconditional assignment at L18, which records the target gid as effective while the real effective gid was not changed. The absent fix is an unconditional return/exit (or an update-only-on-success) in the setgid error branch; the mechanism is a fail-open privilege-decision state (CWE-285).

setuid failure is admitted by the guard `if (setuid (current_user.uid) < 0)` (L5); the only exit is gated by `#if defined (EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE)` (L9) and `if (e == EAGAIN)` (L10), so for any other errno (e.g., EPERM) or an undefined macro the failure path continues to L17 and records the target uid as effective while the real effective uid is unchanged. The absent fix is an unconditional return/exit (or an update-only-on-success) in the setuid error branch; the mechanism is a fail-open privilege-decision state (CWE-285).

assumptions: setuid/setgid returning < 0 leaves the process's effective uid/gid unchanged (standard POSIX semantics).
EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE is not shown as defined, so the exit at L11 cannot be credited as path-excluding.
sys_error's body is unshown and its exit behavior is not attributed; the explicit conditional exit for EAGAIN (L10-L11) indicates the shown code does not rely on sys_error to terminate.
limitations: Caller context is unshown: whether the process runs with elevated effective ids, who populates current_user, and which downstream code consumes current_user.euid/egid are not demonstrated in-fragment, so attacker-triggerability and concrete impact of the failed drop are not shown.
