verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation resolves PRESENT: the pixel and colormap buffers are allocated at capacities that provably dominate the requested read lengths, all ReadBlob counts are equality-checked, colors are capped at 2^bits_per_pixel, dimensions are width>0/height!=0, and each pointer/status is NULL/status-checked before use. No admitted entry-point value reaches an unprotected copy, index, dereference, or decode on the shown types.

evidence.reason: Pixel-buffer capacity rows*MagickMax(bytes_per_line, columns+256) is, for every validated columns/rows (L332-335, width<=0 and height==0 throw; L338-341 bpp whitelist), >= length = bytes_per_line*image->rows computed at L456-457, so the subsequent ReadBlob(image,length,pixels) at L471 cannot write past the allocation; combined with the count-equality check at L471-472 (short reads throw before the buffer is consumed) the failing set is empty, defeating any OOB witness.

Colormap read is bounded by buffer capacity 4*image->colors allocated at L413-414 (packet_size is 3 or 4 so packet_size*colors <= 4*colors) and the read length is exact-checked at L427-428; image->colors itself is <= 2^bits_per_pixel <= 256 for the PseudoClass path by L342-344, so the L435 loop's colormap[i] writes stay within the AcquireImageColormap(colors) capacity (L411).

assumptions: size_t is 64-bit, and width/height originate from signed 32-bit reads (L153-154) so columns*rows*bytes_per_line products (max ~2^62) cannot wrap.
Successful AcquireVirtualMemory/GetVirtualMemoryBlob returns a usable non-NULL buffer (standard ImageMagick semantics), and NULL results are thrown at L465/L486.

DecodeImage writes at most number_pixels bytes into the passed buffer and returns MagickFalse on error, which is checked at L491-496; its pixel count columns*rows fits the buffer capacity rows*max(bytes_per_line, columns+256).
limitations: On a 32-bit size_t platform, bytes_per_line/length (L456-457) and image->columns+256UL (L464) could wrap, and the fragment has no post-computation wrap check (e.g., bytes_per_line < columns*bits_per_pixel/8); that platform model is not established by the shown declarations, so it is demoted here.
The blob-size gate at L458 uses length/8, weaker than a strict length comparison, but the allocation bound L463-464 plus the count check L471-472 neutralize it inside this fragment.
Bitmask shift loops (L553-613) can reach shift counts of 32 on 32-bit operands (UB territory), but the values only feed color arithmetic, not a memory sink.
Extreme dimensions can force huge allocation requests; those fail closed via the NULL checks at L465/L486 rather than admitting an unguarded failure.

verdict.summary: In hfsplus_block_allocate, the allocation (fill) loop advances `offset += PAGE_CACHE_BITS` and reads/kmaps/writes bitmap pages with no `offset >= size` guard (the scan loop has one at L55), so pages outside the size-derived bitmap page range are accessed; with size low bits in 32736..32767 the L25 `end` formula under-counts to `pptr + 0`, forcing the fill to spill the remaining allocation into page index 1 of a single-page bitmap, writing past the bitmap and reporting *max > size (e.g. size=32752, offset=0, *max=32752). Independently, the full-word scan uses the signed `1 << 31`, whose sign-extending `mask >>= 1` falsely marks MSB-set words full and writes wrong bits on fill.

evidence.reason: The fill loop reaches this page-set read with `offset >= size`: `size`, `offset`, and `*max` are unconstrained u32 entry parameters (only `if (!len) return size;` at L11-12), and the only `offset >= size` guard (L55-56) protects the scan loop, not this path (wrong-object drift: L71 guards `start`, not `offset`). With size=32752 (u32 domain, residue 32736..32767 admitted by the L25 formula `((size + 31) & (PAGE_CACHE_BITS - 1)) / 32` = `(32783 & 32767)/32` = 0, so `end = pptr + 0`), a free word 0 is found at L28-36, L71 passes (start=0 < size), `len = min(size - start, len)` = 32752, and after L87 leaves `curr = pptr + 1` the `while (curr < end)` at L90 exits immediately; L101-105 then read page index 1 for a 4094-byte (one-page) bitmap — outside the size-derived page range quoted via `end = pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS / 32;` at L23/L108 — and the loop writes 32720 bits of 0xffffffff (L98) and the partial word (L120) into it, reporting `*max = 65488 > size` at L123. No statement between L103 and L104 constrains `offset`, so the BLOCK test passes. The absent one-statement fix is `if (offset >= size) break;` (or goto out) before this read, mirroring L55-56; without it, an out-of-bounds access beyond the bitmap's valid page range occurs (CWE-787).

Mask initialization is a signed 32-bit left shift into the sign bit (undefined behavior; on two's-complement targets `mask = INT_MIN`), so the subsequent `mask >>= 1` in the L46 scan sign-extends 0x80000000 into 0xC0000000..0xFFFFFFFF; `if (!(n & mask)) goto found;` at L47 then requires all high bits clear, declaring any word with bit 31 set permanently full even when lower bits are free, and the fill path reuses this mask at L78/L82 to set and test the wrong bits, corrupting the on-disk bitmap contents and the allocation count. The identical, correct form `(1U << 31)` appears at L31 and L112 but not at L45, and no protective statement neutralizes the signed shift (CWE-190).

assumptions: Page capacity is PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32 words, quoted verbatim at L23 and L108 (`end = pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS / 32;`).

The valid page range of the bitmap is bounded by `size` (u32 parameter) per the fragment's own boundary convention `if (offset >= size) break;` at L55-56; no other constraint on `size`/`offset`/`*max` is shown.
Bitmap page contents (the `val`/`n` words) are on-disk data and therefore entry-point-controlled; the witness only requires an all-zero first word.
limitations: kmap(page) with an unchecked `read_mapping_page` result (L17-18, L57-59, L104-106) is a candidate NULL/ERR deref, but the NULL/ERR producer is inside the unshown callee, so per the NULL-deref evidence rule it is demoted here.

Behavior of `read_mapping_page` beyond the bitmap file's i_size (NULL vs zero page vs error) is unshown; the decisive harm shown in-fragment is the admitted `offset >= size` page advance and the resulting writes/accounting beyond the size-derived range, which caps severity/confidence.

The signed-shift finding (L45) is technically UB; its observable effect is implementation-dependent, and the wrong-bitmask impact is a correctness/data-integrity issue rather than a memory-safety fault, so it is recorded as secondary (CWE-190).

`HFSPLUS_SB(sb).free_blocks -= *max;` at L124 can underflow as a consequence of the inflated `*max`, but that accounting effect is secondary to the OOB access and is not analyzed as an independent finding.
Callers of this helper are not shown; the witnesses use only values derivable from the fragment (full u32 domains, `if (!len) return size;`), not any caller-supplied invariant.

verdict.summary: The TX packet gather into s->tx_packet is fully constrained: length is checked against remaining buffer space (gem_get_max_buf_len(s, true) minus the already-used offset) immediately before each copy, excluding any length that would reach or pass the buffer bound; no other dangerous operation has a failing witness derivable from the shown code.

evidence.reason: This guard resolves the only dangerous operation with a shown failure set (the copy at lines 63-65 into s->tx_packet, and the pointer advance at line 66) as PRESENT: it admits only tx_desc_get_length(desc) <= gem_get_max_buf_len(s, true) - (p - s->tx_packet) and breaks otherwise, so offset + length never exceeds the max buffer length; the guarded expression is the exact value the sink consumes, with no intervening modification (Guard-Identity Audit: no drift), and the degenerate case offset == max_buf_len forces any length >= 1 to break. The BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach, so no OOB witness survives; the desc/desc_first reads and tx_desc_addr stores lack any shown capacity or in-fragment producer to exceed it, and all format strings are literals.

assumptions: gem_get_max_buf_len(s, true) is the capacity bound of the tx gather buffer s->tx_packet; the guard at lines 50-58 uses it as the remaining-space bound and no shown line contradicts it.
desc and desc_first are arrays of DESC_MAX_NUM_WORDS uint32_t words (lines 3 and 71).
limitations: gem_get_desc_len(s, false) is not bounded within the fragment; a write past desc[DESC_MAX_NUM_WORDS] would require that helper to return more than DESC_MAX_NUM_WORDS, which no shown statement can drive (callee body unshown), so the candidate is demoted.
The allocation size of s->tx_packet and the capacity of s->tx_desc_addr[] are not declared in the shown fragment.
The MemTxResult of address_space_read is discarded, and a failed read could leave desc stale, but the fragment shows no failure path that dereferences such stale data.

The inner while loop could rescan guest-owned descriptors, but each non-breaking iteration advances p by at least one byte and the size guard bounds the total, so an unbounded-loop witness is not demonstrable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with a demonstrable failure set is protected by a statement that survives the BREAK test: the lookbehind length stores (lines 1583, 1588) are bound by the check at lines 1567-1570 (admitted deltanext in [0,255], sum <= 255, so the U8 store cannot truncate); the repeatcpy write (1217-1219) is exactly covered by SvGROW(last_str, (mincount * l) + 1) at line 1216; the min-length accumulation is guarded by FAIL("Regexp out of space") at lines 1032-1035. No in-fragment NULL producer exists for the data dereferences, and OOB candidates on arrays whose capacities are not shown in the fragment are demoted. No ABSENT sink with a surviving witness.

evidence.reason: The lookbehind length store is PRESENT-protected: every path reaching it passes the guard at lines 1567-1570 (deltanext < 0 || deltanext > (I32)U8_MAX || minnext > (I32)U8_MAX || minnext + deltanext > (I32)U8_MAX) with FAIL2 aborting otherwise, admitting only deltanext in [0,255] and minnext+deltanext <= 255; with minnext >= 0 from the shown non-negative accumulations (min = 0, line 20), (U8)minnext + deltanext is at most 255 and is stored without truncation, so the sink's failure set (truncated U8 length) has no surviving witness and the BREAK test passes (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach).

The repeatcpy write is PRESENT-protected: it writes l bytes (mincount - 1) times starting at offset l, i.e. mincount*l total bytes, and the immediately preceding SvGROW at line 1216 reserves (mincount * l) + 1 bytes, exactly the payload plus the trailing NUL slot, on every path taken under 'if (mincount > 1)'; the BREAK test passes because the maximum write (mincount*l) is strictly below the quoted capacity (mincount*l)+1 and no shown value can wrap the 64-bit product on a reachable input, so no OOB witness survives.

assumptions: min (and hence every recursive study_chunk return minnext) is non-negative: initialized to 0 at line 20 and incremented only by shown non-negative operands (min += l, min += min1, min += minnext * mincount), consistent with assert(min >= 0).
The regnode chain is structurally well-formed: the main loop (line 83) terminates at END/last, and branch/trie walks advance via regnext.
limitations: The lookbehind guard at lines 1567-1570 does not exclude a negative minnext, but no shown statement can produce one (JOIN_EXACT and the recursive bodies are unshown), so such a witness is not derivable in-fragment.

SvGROW's (mincount * l) + 1 capacity could in principle wrap only if the 64-bit product overflowed, which would require a last_found substring near 2^32 bytes built from a regex of comparable size; no shown cap exists, but no demonstrated witness is constructible.

OOB on RExC_open_parens, RExC_close_parens, RExC_recurse, RExC_study_chunk_recursed (bitmap), and trie->jump cannot be assessed because their capacities are declared outside the fragment (CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE); demoted.

'l -= old' at line ~1207 and the (s + old), l read assume the unshown data-structure invariant old <= SvCUR(last_found); only assert(old >= 0) is shown, and an in-fragment violating producer cannot be derived.

data == NULL combined with SCF_DO_SUBSTR or SCF_DO_STCLASS_OR would fault at lines 24/1961/1973, but the only in-fragment NULL call site passes flags = 0, so no NULL-producing path exists inside the fragment; NULL from an unshown caller is out of scope.
Return values discarded at the DEFINEP/CURLYM study_chunk calls are length heuristics only; no shown sink consumes a failed status from them.

verdict.summary: S_study_chunk's signed delta accumulation `delta += (minnext + deltanext) * maxcount - minnext * mincount` (lines 1034-1035) can wrap SSize_t because the FAIL guard at lines 1021-1022 bounds only mincount/min and the is_inf shortcut at lines 1028-1029 excludes only deltanext==SSize_t_MAX or maxcount==REG_INFTY; a finite large maxcount such as 4294967295 with minnext+deltanext ~ 4294967295 yields a product ~1.84e19 exceeding SSize_t_MAX, corrupting delta (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: maxcount is assigned from unbound ARG2(scan) at line 927 and keeps the full SSize_t domain from the declaration at line 844; the FAIL guard at lines 1021-1022 exhibits wrong-object drift for this sink (it constrains mincount and min, not maxcount), and the is_inf shortcut at lines 1028-1029 admits every finite maxcount less than REG_INFTY; with minnext=1, mincount=1, and a nested quantifier producing deltanext=4294967294, maxcount=4294967295 makes (1+4294967294)*4294967295-1 ~ 1.8446744e19 > 9.223372e18 (SSize_t_MAX), a signed overflow that wraps the delta used for RExC_maxlen/pos_delta; the absent one-statement fix is a bound check on maxcount (or clamping delta to SSize_t_MAX) before the multiplication (CWE-190).

assumptions: REG_INFTY equals the SSize_t maximum, so a finite maxcount of 4294967295 does not equal REG_INFTY and does not take the is_inf branch at lines 1028-1029; REG_INFTY's value is not shown in the fragment.
ARG1/ARG2 return the quantifier counts stored in the compiled regnode, derived from attacker-controlled regex text, and no statement in the fragment bounds them.
limitations: Capacity for RExC_recurse, RExC_open_parens/RExC_close_parens, RExC_study_chunk_recursed, and trie->jump is not declared in the fragment, so OOB candidates on those arrays are demoted for lack of capacity evidence.
The stopmin inconsistency at line 211 (`stopmin > minnext` compared against assignment `stopmin = min + min1`) is a logic discrepancy whose security impact is not demonstrable within the fragment.
Downstream memory-safety effects of the wrapped delta (e.g., RExC_maxlen consumers) occur outside the shown fragment.

verdict.summary: ELF parser trusts unvalidated file-derived header fields: 'dynamic'/'dynstr' are used uninitialized when no matching section exists, and unchecked e_shoff/e_shnum/e_shstrndx/sh_size/d_val offsets index the mmap'd file beyond its st.st_size capacity, causing out-of-bounds reads.

evidence.reason: 'dynamic' is declared at line 335 without an initializer and assigned only inside the conditional at lines 342-344, so an attacker-supplied ELF without a matching '.dynamic' section leaves it indeterminate; line 349 consumes it as the index into 'shdr' with no prior initialization or bounds check, and 'count' at line 350 is derived from the same indeterminate entry (shdr[dynamic].sh_size), so the subsequent dyn[i] reads are also out of bounds against the mmap capacity st.st_size (line 23). Missing fix: initialize 'dynamic'/'dynstr' and validate the index plus table extent before use. Primary CWE-457; OOB read follows.

Attacker-controlled 'e_shoff' (line 176) and 'e_shstrndx' (max 65535) are unconstrained by any shown check; the read at 'elf_map + e_shoff + e_shstrndx*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr)' can exceed the quoted mapping capacity st.st_size (line 23). The checked call 'validated_offset' at line 184 executes after this line and constrains only 'name', so it does not protect this sink. Missing fix: 'e_shstrndx < e_shnum' plus 'e_shoff + e_shnum*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) <= st.st_size'. CWE-125.

The loop at line 182 admits i in [0, e_shnum-1] with 'e_shnum' attacker-controlled and no check that the section table fits in the mapping (st.st_size, line 23), so 'shdr[i]' dereferences beyond the map for a small file with a large e_shnum. The 'validated_offset' guard at line 184 protects only 'name', not 'shdr[i]' (wrong-object drift). Missing fix: bound the table extent before the loop. CWE-125.

assumptions: The mmap'd region's capacity is st.st_size bytes, quoted at line 23.
ELF header fields (e_shoff, e_shnum, e_shstrndx, e_phnum, sh_size, d_val) and section/dynamic table contents are entry-point file data with no shown constraint.
limitations: The strcpy(&name[15 - 6], "[...]") at line 259 writes at name[9..14], within the string extent implied by the prior successful strlen(name) > 15 check, and safe-in-bounds by that extent; the exact coverage of 'validated_offset' (unshown body) is not attributed.
flag2str_sh/flag2str write into char flag[4] (line 8) with unshown bodies; no overflow can be confirmed from the fragment.
The 64-bit branch duplicates the same sinks; findings are cited once on the 32-bit numbered copy.
Reading ehdr fields at line 36+ without a minimum-size check is the same unguarded over-read class and is subsumed by the reported findings.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with a demonstrable failure set in the fragment carries a protective check; the array-indexing by unconstrained cnt/tablenr and the fields->head() deref cannot be confirmed as failures because no capacity or NULL-producing statement is shown in the fragment, and the two dereferences that follow allocation/failure-prone calls are guarded by explicit NULL/return checks.

assumptions: DBUG_ASSERT(fields->elements) at line 18 is debug-only and provides no runtime protection in release builds.

The do/while at lines 108-128 executes at least once (tbl initialized to table at line 107) and all push_back/new failures return early (lines 123-124, 126-127), so temp_fields.elements >= 1 and both func_count = elements - 1 (line 139) and head_ref() (line 135) are safe.
tbl->alias.c_ptr() (line 111) returns a NUL-terminated string per standard LEX_STRING semantics, making strlen (line 112) safe.
limitations: Capacities of tmp_table_param, tmp_tables, fields_for_table, and join->map2table are not declared or allocated anywhere in the fragment, so per the CAPACITY-EVIDENCE RULE the OOB candidates at lines 95, 130, 144-146, 47, and 119 are demoted in both directions; no OOB verdict is possible.

A NULL result from fields->head() at line 24 requires an empty fields list, which is a caller-supplied state not produced by any shown statement (only the debug assert and a comment mention it), so the NULL-deref candidate is a limitation, not a confirmed vulnerability.
join->join_tab and map2table entries could be NULL only via unshown caller state; no in-fragment producer exists, so those derefs are not findings.
No bound check on cnt exists at lines 95/130/144-146, but no in-fragment capacity establishes a failing value; a witness of cnt >= capacity is not derivable from the fragment alone.
